title: Editor E8 slice: the last seven tool_use readers read model output through a schema
detail:
Split from PROG-E8 on 2026-11-16. The rest of that row's item (4): the seven tool_use readers PROG-E8B listed as still on hand-written ladders, outside the Vera and builder paths. No migration, no UI change, no model call in any test.

PREMISE RE-TESTED FIRST (ADR-1082). All seven were found on main and all seven still read model output by hand. Five walked it with typeof ladders (lib/whatsapp/extract.ts coerceItem with its refs, housing and event readers; lib/importer/vision.ts inline in planSeedImages; lib/launch/buildout.ts applyPolish; lib/connections/normalize.ts coerceExtraction and coerceContactDetails; lib/events/normalize.ts coerceEventExtraction and coerceEventDetails). Two did not check it at all: lib/importer/extract/run.ts cast block.input to RawExtraction, and lib/listing-seeder/extract.ts cast it to the listing shape for lib/listing-seeder/coerce.ts, so a wrong-typed value reached a .trim() and threw. In the importer that throw was caught and the whole extraction was lost; in the listing seeder nothing caught it (app/(main)/admin/listing-seeder/actions.ts calls the coercer outside a try).

WHAT CHANGED (the ADR-1287 pattern, lib/ai/schema.ts validateModelValue plus a zod schema, exactly as the five PROG-E8B readers do). Each reader is now a schema that says what every raw field may be and what a wrong one reads as, plus a small mapper that builds the stored shape. lib/ai/schema.ts gains the six blocks they share: aliasedText (a field with an older key beside it), looseEnum, looseNumber, rowsOrNone, unitBox and citedField. lib/events/normalize.ts: every reader in the file (event, details, box, corners, quality, domain, date). lib/connections/extraction.ts (new): the card readers moved here out of lib/connections/normalize.ts, which three client components import for tag and crop helpers, so the schema library is NOT added to their bundle; normalize.ts keeps only those browser helpers. lib/whatsapp/extract.ts: one ITEMS_REPLY schema for the batch. lib/importer/extract/reply.ts (new) readRawExtraction, called by run.ts in place of the cast. lib/importer/vision.ts PLAN_REPLY. lib/listing-seeder/extract.ts readListingReply: extractListing reads the tool input through the kind's schema in place of the cast, so the coercer only ever receives well-typed parts. lib/launch/buildout.ts POLISH_REPLY (imported by relative path so scripts/probes/launch-buildout.mjs can still load the file under node). WHERE TWO OF THE SCHEMAS SIT, and why: lib/importer/extract/coerce.ts and lib/listing-seeder/coerce.ts are each loaded on their own by an older probe (LIVE-1346 importer-authorship, LIVE-1396 listing-source-copy) that allows them no new import, so those two files are unchanged and the schema read sits one step earlier, at the call that receives the tool input. The event description keeps its own line (str(r.description, 8000), now schema-backed) because LIVE-860's probe pins that line.

BEHAVIOUR. On a valid reply every reader returns what it returned before. That was measured, not assumed: before any change, 19,389 payloads (a rich valid reply per reader, then every field at every depth replaced by each of 24 junk values) were run through the readers on main and the outputs saved; after the change the same payloads were run again and compared byte for byte. The battery was a scratch harness and is not committed. Every reply that differs is a malformed one, and each difference is toward tolerance, never a new throw: (a) listing seeder, 316 fuzz cases that THREW on main now give a draft with the bad part left out, and a reply that is not an object gives the empty draft the operator completes (the AI-off path); (b) importer extract, 684 cases where one wrong-typed part or a null list row lost the whole extraction (null, a name-only draft) now lose only that part, and a reply that is not an object is null as a failed call is (on main a bare number, string or array, which the SDK never sends as tool input, gave a name-only draft); (c) image plan, a null row no longer voids the whole plan (13 cases); it is dropped like any other unusable row; (d) WhatsApp import, a row that is itself an array is dropped instead of becoming a blank 'other' item with no refs (27 cases); (e) a cover, photo or logo imageIndex of Infinity (JSON 1e999) reads as 0 instead of Infinity (3 cases).

NONE WAS LEFT BEHIND AS TOO RISKY. None of the seven is on a payment, email-send or auth path. The closest is applyPolish, which can rewrite the first-email draft a person reviews: its output still goes through enforceCites unchanged, it sends nothing, and its fuzz outputs are identical to main on all 1,081 payloads.

VERIFIED: the fuzz comparison above; unit tests per reader for a valid and a malformed reply (lib/events/normalize.test.ts, lib/whatsapp/extract.test.ts and lib/importer/extract/run.test.ts are new; connections, vision, listing seeder extract, buildout and schema tests extended), with the model seam mocked wherever a test goes through a call; the four older probes that load these files (launch-buildout, listing-source-copy, importer-authorship, ai-coaching-consequences) still pass; lint, scoped typecheck and the contract guards. NOT VERIFIED: no reader was run against a real model reply or in a browser, and the bundle size of the three connections client components was not measured (the import that would have grown it was avoided by the file split, and the probe checks that normalize.ts imports no schema).

STILL ON A HAND LADDER, on purpose, and not a read of raw tool output: lib/launch/buildout.ts readStoredBuildout (reads our own stored jsonb); lib/connections/normalize.ts normalizeTag and dedupeTags (shared with the browser, fed typed strings by the schema reader); and the checks inside lib/importer/extract/coerce.ts and lib/listing-seeder/coerce.ts, which now run on schema-typed data and also re-check stored drafts.

verify.note: Fails on main: lib/ai/schema.ts has none of the extractor blocks, and each of the seven readers walks the raw tool input with typeof tests or a cast. It loads the real modules (scripts/probe-ts.mjs) and runs them: passes once the blocks hold on malformed values, the four pure readers (launch polish, event scan, card scan, importer extract) give the stored shape on a valid reply and their safe fallback on malformed ones without throwing (the importer case threw on main), each of the seven hands its input to validateModelValue with a schema and carries no ladder, the card reader lives outside the client-imported helpers, and a valid and a malformed test exist per reader with the model seam mocked.
